title: How to Use the HSI in Microsoft Flight Simulator | MSFS A-Z (Letter H)
description:
Master the Horizontal Situation Indicator (HSI) in Microsoft Flight Simulator and eliminate reverse sensing forever. Learn how to track VOR radials and nail localizer back course approaches in the Cessna 172 G1000 NXi without mental math.

Flying blind in solid IMC can turn a standard instrument approach into a fragmented guessing game on a traditional split-gauge six-pack. In this episode of Microsoft Flight Simulator A to Z (Letter H), we break down why the Horizontal Situation Indicator (HSI) is one of the most critical evolutions in instrument flight navigation.

We take the default Cessna 172 Skyhawk equipped with the Working Title Garmin G1000 NXi into low-visibility clouds over the North Sea and Rotterdam The Hague Airport (EHRD). You will learn how the HSI overlays course deviation directly onto a motorized compass card for an intuitive bird’s-eye perspective. We demonstrate how to intercept the Rotterdam VOR (110.40 RTM), configure the HSI map overlay, and apply the universal "Front Course Rule" to fly a Localizer Back Course to Runway 06 with zero reverse sensing. Finally, discover how the G1000's cyan ground track vector diamond eliminates crab-angle guesswork in severe crosswinds.
